name: @legion/envoy-client
//: test: each command's --timeout is at least twice the slowest row or hook it ran under 8 busy loops on 2 CPUs at 61b66deb (three runs in a builds Job).

The first, 30000: a ! command in envoy.json > still running after 10 s is an error naming the field and the file, 10,200.35 ms; the two keyed-writes upload rows, as fixed after that head, took up to 10,440 ms under the same load in an issue pod. Read again at 6ca1a534 with #4437's fourth merge, the whole command under the same load (two runs in builds Job d8-ec-first-8): the files main's #4140 gave row timeouts of their own, the slowest nats-credential-deadlines.test.ts's switch whose first trade answers 503, 12,599.24 ms. Read again at the round-3 class-search tree (main 46c275dcba with #4437's head e9d8f5075f and its uncommitted fixes), the whole command under the same load (two runs in builds Job d2-c9-ec, 2026-11-19): followNatsCredential's switch whose first trade answers 503 waits for ready, 8,900.18 and 14,991.18 ms, which 30000 holds 2.001 times; Bun prints no hook times, so no hook is read there. Main's nats-handshake.test.ts (#4353) runs here since its rows read the timers its dials arm, not the wall clock: under the same load (three runs in each of builds Jobs nt-t1-8 and nt-c1-8, 2026-11-20, beside nats-dial-retry.test.ts), its slowest row, a server that never answers, which waits out its dial's whole 10 s bound on the process's clock, took up to 10,104.52 ms, which 30000 holds 2.968 times; nats-dial-retry.test.ts's slowest, the last dial's own error, up to 623.22 ms. Read again at #4437's round-4 tree 24b2e96b28, with nats-handshake.test.ts and nats-dial-retry.test.ts as e61fe76646 rewrote them, the whole command under the same load (three runs in builds Job g4b-ec-first, legion-load-run-hbzpt, 2026-11-21, with LEGION_E2E=1 as CI sets it, each hook timed by a preload the Job's patch added): the slowest row, that switch whose first trade answers 503, 13,404.06 ms (12,298.89 and 10,017.98 ms the slowest of the other runs), which 30000 holds 2.24 times; the slowest hook, the temporary-directory afterEach dispatch-review.test.ts registers, 84.15 ms; nats-handshake.test.ts's slowest row, the server that never answers, at most 10,003.17 ms, and nats-dial-retry.test.ts's, the last dial's own error, at most 555.16 ms.

The second, 120000: 6,202.12 ms here; with LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK and LEGION_E2E_DISPATCH_STACK set, nats-stall.test.ts's slowest row took 50,109.26 ms and the live suites' beforeAll up to 52,389.38 ms under the same load. nats-auth.test.ts's Docker rows took at most 32.89 ms on CI. Three files of main's #4140 run here too, each above the first's half: dispatch-write-outcomes.test.ts, whose every sequence of events took 16,382.88 ms in the first command under that load (d8-ec-first-8); broker-credential-signins.test.ts, whose closed client's slot took 16,094.57 ms (d8-ec-moved-8); and nats-credential.test.ts, whose rows behind the auth service, with LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK set, took up to 20,483.92 ms (builds Jobs d8-natscred-8 and d8-natscred-8b). That file's beforeAll, one go build of natsd and calloutd, keeps a guard of its own (BUILD_GUARD_MS, 300000): at least twice the 56 s the CI step running the file whole took at its longest, over its 57 green runs up to 2026-11-19. Read again there (the same Job and load, with LEGION_E2E_ENVOY_STACK and LEGION_E2E_DISPATCH_STACK set): nats-stall.test.ts's row B, 50,099.84 and 50,101.21 ms, the slowest; broker-credential-signins.test.ts 16,091.73 ms; nats-credential.test.ts's reconnect after two refusals 13,685.66 ms here and up to 20,010.78 ms alone (the envoy-session-stall step's command); dispatch-write-outcomes.test.ts 12,192.64 ms; the live suites' new row, a plan a person approved names dispatch plan-approve, 1,798.60 ms. dispatch-askgate.test.ts's row that spawns node -e fails in a builds Job, which has no node; CI's runner has one. Main's third live suite, comment-mention.live.test.ts (#4426), runs here beside the other two: its beforeAll starts the same stack (startDispatchStack), and the envoy-session-stall step that runs it whole took at most 16 s over its 7 green merge-group runs up to 2026-11-20 (44709419415 to 44735067614). Read under the same load at 1c711353dc, the file alone (three runs in builds Job r4b-mention-8, legion-load-run-dp4j4, 2026-11-21, with LEGION_E2E_DISPATCH_STACK set and each hook timed by a print the Job's patch added, since Bun prints no hook times): its beforeAll took 50,287.16 ms and 47,893.23 ms with the Go build cache an earlier build left (twice: 100,574.32 ms, which 120000 holds), its afterAll at most 10,703.09 ms and its row at most 1,905.42 ms. The Job's first run, on an empty Go cache, built the server cold in a beforeAll of 466,790.72 ms, which 120000 does not hold: every live suite here builds the same server, so a run of this command with the stack variables set on an empty Go cache has its first live suite pay that build. CI's envoy-client job runs this command with neither variable set, so its live suites skip there; the envoy-session-stall job, which sets both, builds natsd, the listener and the Dispatch server in a step of its own before its first suite, so each suite's build there is warm.
